turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mrs. Iyer, come, sit. I am Dr. Menon. You look tired. Tell me, what brought you today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): What brought me. My feet only. They are swollen, and I am tired of the whole thing. We waited forty minutes outside.

[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, I am Meera, her daughter. I live with her and I set the pill box. Both ankles have been puffy for about three weeks, and she gets breathless walking to the gate.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks, four weeks, what is the difference. It is there. She will narrate my whole life if you allow her.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both ankles, and short of breath on walking. I am noting that. Any chest pain along with the breathlessness?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. Don't make a big file out of it.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will not call that chest pain, then. Any cough, or any fever at home?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough. No fever. I am not lying here dying, am I.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She is washed out, Doctor, even in the chair she says there is no energy. Sleep itself is okay, she is not confused.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright. Passing urine, any burning or very little urine?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Urine is fine. Why so many questions, my head is already heavy. No, not headache, I am just irritated.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fair enough, no headache. There is pitting swelling on both ankles. Lungs are clear, no crackles. Heart sounds are normal and I don't hear a murmur.

[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is eighty-four. Blood pressure is one-forty-two over eighty-eight. Oxygen saturation is ninety-seven percent. Skin is not warm, so no fever to the touch, though I have not used a thermometer.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): One-forty-two. The other doctor said it was low and he stopped some tablet. I cannot keep all these numbers in my head.

[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That was Dr. Shah at the hospital, about six weeks back. He stopped atorvastatin twenty milligrams at night, the cholesterol tablet, because her calves were cramping. She has not swallowed it since.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): So atorvastatin twenty milligrams is stopped, and I am not restarting it today. Are the cramps still there, or did they settle?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Settled. After he stopped it. Don't start that one again, the legs were paining enough.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good, cramps settled, statin stays off. Now I need what is actually going into her mouth. Meera, talk me through the box.

[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Morning she gets the blood pressure tablet, telmisartan forty milligrams. Then the water tablet. And there is a little white one also, which is where I got confused.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not the same tablet. She double puts things and then blames me. I just swallow and keep quiet.

[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mummy, please. The little white one is the telmisartan itself, same strip. Last week I did put it twice, morning and again at lunch, by mistake. From Monday it is only once.

[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me think this aloud. So the little white one and the BP tablet are one medicine, telmisartan forty milligrams, once each morning. It was double-counted last week, not now. We will not list it twice. Is that right?
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, Doctor. Only once now.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): If both of you say so. I don't have the energy to fight about a white tablet.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the water tablet, what strength are you giving?
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Furosemide forty milligrams, one in the morning. I have written forty on the box.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no. That man said twenty milligram. Forty is too strong, I will be in the toilet the whole day. Write twenty.

[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm. Daughter says forty milligrams, you say twenty milligram, and the strip is not in front of me. I cannot honestly tell which dose is in that box. Any other regular medicine? Something for sugar, or pain?

[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No sugar medicine. No pain tablet daily. She has been on BP treatment for five-ish years, that is as exact as I can be. The statin we already stopped, so don't count that also.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Five years, ten years. My husband had pressure also. He is gone. What is the use of counting years.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am sorry. We will not force an exact year. Any medicine allergy, either of you?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. I have said it again and again.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No known allergy. She has taken penicillin before, no rash, nothing.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): The swelling, is it worse by evening? Do the legs ache?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Evening it is more, and they ache, yes. If I put the legs up, morning is a little better. Still ugly to look at.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Better with the legs up. Have you noticed weight going up? Waking at night gasping for air?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Weight I don't know. Gasping at night, no. I sleep. Don't add things.

[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No recent weight at home. She eats less because she says the food is bland. She has been irritable since this swelling, snaps at small things. That part is not new-new, but it is more now.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Putting this together, my working impression is extra fluid, ankle swelling from water retention, possibly a bit of strain on the heart, and I am not confirming heart failure today. Well, actually I almost said heart failure, and I should not. The muddled water tablet is part of the problem.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Then don't say that word. Just do something. And this fan is rattling, I cannot even hear you properly.

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): See, the thing is, I am going to change one medicine and leave the rest. Telmisartan forty milligrams once in the morning stays. I will set the water tablet as furosemide forty milligrams, one tablet by mouth every morning. Stop whatever water tablet is in the box and use only this.
[SEG0042] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So forty milligrams once every morning, old water tablets out. Before food or after?

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): After breakfast, once only. It will make her pass more urine for a few hours, that is expected, so please don't skip it. If she is very giddy on standing, or the swelling goes above the knee, or she is breathless even at rest, come earlier. Otherwise I will see her in two weeks.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. More walking. Forty milligram and the toilet nonstop. I am already fed up.

[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I know it is tiring. I am also sending bloods today, kidney function and the salts, because we are fixing the water tablet. Lab is downstairs, they will do it before you go home.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will take her. Just so the file is right, BP for five-ish years, she lives with me, I cook and I do the medicines. She has never smoked.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. I don't drink also. Once in a while coffee, then I cannot sleep, that is all. Can we finish.

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Noted. No smoking, no alcohol, and she lives with her daughter. High blood pressure is ongoing, roughly five years, not an exact date. No new tablet besides the water tablet change, and the statin remains stopped.

[SEG0049] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Clear. One white tablet only, that is telmisartan once. Water tablet is the new forty milligrams every morning. Statin stays stopped. We will do the blood test now.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine, let us go. My legs are paining and I am tired of this chair.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Meera, legs up in the evening, less salt in the food, and no extra tablet from the old box. I will see you in two weeks with the report.
